scope: Verified only the PDF program constraints against local ISO 32000-2:2020 sponsored EC3 text: 9.6.3, 9.6.5.1/2/4, 9.7.4.1/2/3, 9.9.1/2, Tables 124/125. Binary layouts, algorithms and numeric format limits in Type 1 (including Supplement 5015), CFF 5176, Type 2 5177, TrueType Reference Manual and OpenType/ISO 14496-22:2019 remain pending primary-text review. Project resource budgets are not ISO requirements; independently written generators alone are not specification verification.

requirements.status: TrueType/OpenType glyf outlines, cmap 0/2/4/6/10/12/13, exact subtable identities, hmtx and post; internal layouts pending primary-text review
requirements.gaps: Other cmap/post formats and collections are unsupported. Format 14 UVS does not change single-code PDF glyph selection and is intentionally not used. Instruction dependencies require TrueType primary review.

verification.rule: Require the six glyf-program tables, keep PDF-selected (3,1) distinct from (3,10) and platform 0, and ignore font vertical tables for PDF metrics.
verification.verdict: corrected: exact Unicode subtable identities were conflated; program-layer constraints now agree with the ISO text and minimized expectations
verification.implementation: Requires glyf/head/hhea/hmtx/loca/maxp; separates (3,1), (3,10), and platform 0; allows cmap-free CID programs; ignores vhea/vmtx.
verification.expectations: Required-table rejection, cmap identity and ignored-vertical-table fixtures derive from these ISO rules; low-level outline/cmap binary interpretations remain pending.
verification.outside: PdfFont::load must enforce cmap presence for simple fonts and absence for CIDFontType2, instruction-dependent auxiliary tables, and table-preservation obligations. PdfFont glyph selection must choose the single (3,0) high-byte range before lookup and use (1,0)/post fallbacks per 9.6.5.4.
pending: TrueType Reference Manual: table layouts, quadratics, composites, cmap and post binary formats, instruction dependencies
OpenType / ISO/IEC 14496-22:2019: sfnt layouts, cmap identities beyond PDF-selected encodings, newer cmap formats
verification.evidence: ISO-derived PDF constraints plus analytic binary fixtures. Secondary read-fonts 0.41.0 comparison agrees on 26 cmap 10/13 code queries. Its mapping API does not implement format 2; no differential claim for format 2 or a primary-format known-answer dataset.
verification.choices: Platform 0 and (3,10) are exposed separately; supplementary Unicode mappings never impersonate PDF (3,1). Format 14 is unused because 9.6.5.4 selects by a single mapped value, while 9.7.4.2 uses explicit CIDs/GIDs. Legacy component offsets use unscaled translation; external semantics pending.

requirements.status: CFF/CID CFF, all 391 standard SIDs, ISOAdobe/Expert/ExpertSubset and custom charsets, Standard/Expert/custom encodings, FDSelect 0/3/4, default CFF2 charstring and Private DICT blends; external definitions pending primary review
requirements.gaps: Nondefault variations, CFF2 Font DICT matrices and arbitrary PostScript are unsupported. All low-level CFF/Type 2/CFF2 definitions remain pending primary-text review despite analytic and secondary evidence.

verification.rule: Embed one CFF font, use charset CIDs for CID-keyed CFF and direct GIDs otherwise, and require CFF plus cmap rather than glyf tables for OpenType CFF.
verification.verdict: corrected: OpenType CFF was incorrectly required to contain the glyf branch metrics/header tables; PDF-minimum CFF+cmap fonts now agree with the text
verification.implementation: Rejects multiple CFF fonts, resolves nonidentity charset CIDs, requires cmap for OpenType CFF, and uses charstring advances when optional hmtx/hhea are absent.
verification.expectations: Single-font, nonidentity CID, minimal OpenType and missing-cmap cases agree with ISO; INDEX/DICT/charstring binary encodings and CFF2 are not verified by ISO.
verification.outside: PdfFont::load must validate FontFile3 subtype/dictionary compatibility, omit CFF Length1/2/3 entries, and retain direct-GID selection for non-CID CFF as already implemented.
pending: Adobe Technical Note 5176: INDEX, DICT, charsets, predefined encodings and SID tables, FDArray/FDSelect
Adobe Technical Note 5177: Type 2 operators, widths, flex, seac, subroutines and stack limits
OpenType / ISO/IEC 14496-22:2019: CFF2, variation stores and blend semantics
verification.evidence: Secondary read-fonts 0.41.0 comparison: 668 glyph-name mappings and 1792 code mappings across the seven metadata fixtures agree, with undefined entries normalized against GID 0; the gap at ExpertEncoding code 92 was corrected following that comparison. Analytic fixtures exercise FDSelect 4 and Private DICT blends; no external known-answer dataset or primary-format verification. Secondary skrifa 0.46.2 agrees on bounds and curve counts of six default CFF2 glyphs: static, charstring blend, inherited/overridden Private DICT blends, FDSelect 4 and FD index 256. Font DICT matrix behavior disagreed and is explicitly unsupported; these comparisons are not primary-text verification.
verification.choices: CFF2 uses default normalized coordinates only; Private DICT vsindex initializes charstring variation selection, which a charstring vsindex can override (secondary skrifa 0.46.2 agreement, pending primary review). CFF2 Font DICT matrices return explicit Unsupported after a secondary disagreement. Random is deterministic 0.5 and flex retains curves; external semantics remain pending.

requirements.status: Type 1 PFA/PFB framing, eexec and charstring ciphers, subroutines, flex and seac
requirements.gaps: Static dictionary extraction; computed PostScript dictionaries and custom OtherSubrs are unsupported.

verification.rule: Type 1 exposes named glyphs and a built-in encoding with .notdef; ignore PaintType and constrain PDF eexec to binary.
verification.verdict: agrees at the generic program layer; PDF embedding restrictions require caller enforcement
verification.implementation: Requires .notdef and an encoding; returns the same geometry regardless of PaintType; supports standalone PFA hex and PFB as generic reader extensions.
verification.expectations: Missing-.notdef rejection and PaintType-invariant outline follow the ISO text; hex/PFB successes are standalone-format tests, not valid-PDF claims.
verification.outside: PdfFont::load/program must validate FontFile Length1/2/3 boundaries and binary-only eexec; enforce subset naming and encoding fallback to .notdef at the PDF dictionary layer.
pending: Adobe Type 1 Font Format: PFA/PFB framing, ciphers, static dictionaries, charstrings, flex and hint replacement
Adobe Technical Note 5015, Type 1 Font Format Supplement: supplemented Type 1 programs
verification.evidence: Analytic outlines and independently authored binary fixtures only; no differential run or external known-answer dataset has been used.

requirements.status: Bounded parsers and outlines; exact linear operator/segment budgets, branching-subroutine exhaustion, prefix and expanded format mutation tests
requirements.gaps: Budget violations are syntax errors with standalone-buffer positions; malformed outlines are reported lazily.

verification.rule: Bound every font parse and outline by explicit budgets; reject exhaustion with a buffer position.
verification.verdict: project policy tested; removed the unsupported claim that ISO 9.9 specifies these budgets
verification.implementation: Caps bytes, values, glyphs, operations, segments and recursion; positions syntax failures in the relevant font buffer.
verification.expectations: Hostile vectors and mutation tests assert project budgets and failure positions, independently of any ISO numeric limit.
verification.outside: No shared API change required; dedicated font fuzz target remains future work.
pending: Adobe Type 1 Font Format: normative Type 1 operand stack limits
Adobe Technical Note 5177 and OpenType CFF2: normative operand/subroutine limits
verification.evidence: Project-policy fixtures measure exact operation/segment budgets for 64/128/256-line glyphs with and without subroutines; branching recursion and mutation tests exercise shared exhaustion. No claim that ISO 9.9 specifies numeric budgets.
